paragraphs: In Kiddushin 81a he said to Rav Ashi, “The master, too, should be flogged,” etc. Yuchasin reads ben Perata, while Seder HaDorot reads R' Nachman of Parpatya.[^1]

notes.text: פא. gives 81a by convention without a fresh edition check. ס״הד is contextually Seder HaDorot, not a newly verified work identity; ר״נ is contextually Nachman with title R', not inherited Rav from the separate heading. Perhatya retains ה; ben Perata and Parpatya preserve the actual different forms, without harmonizing relation or place identity. Full Rav remains for the heading and Ashi; מר is the direct-address master, not an instruction that the master flog someone. Source וכו׳ remains etc.
